text: The sediment study from Ostrava Lake was conducted by the Sarnow Institute, according to a report filed this week with the Ministry of Civic Science. The paper, dated March 14 and signed by lead researcher Elin Varga, analyzed core samples taken over 18 months and concluded that the lake’s lower strata preserved a continuous industrial record from 1962 to 2008. The institute said it recovered 214 samples from three drilling sites and identified sharply elevated nickel and soot markers in the deepest band. Ministry officials confirmed receipt of the report and said the Sarnow team’s findings would inform a broader environmental review of the Ostrava basin.
